findings.finding: The precedence sentence added for R2-2 reads 'Assigned only when no other mode applies: an index, a planned baseline or a reference design keeps its mode, and its licence ceiling binds'. It now contradicts five records and the checker. Arize-ai/phoenix, yuzhenmao/DeLM, mattermost/mattermost, qzzqzzb/Self-Harness and the OPHSD repository are all used as design references. Their own texts say 'design reference only' or 'semantics only', and phoenix's 'what' calls it 'a reference for MAS-RA-003's mapping'. Under the sentence as written they should keep REFERENCE_DESIGN, yet all five are LICENSE_BLOCKED. The checker forbids REFERENCE_DESIGN for them: REUSE_OUTCOMES admits REFERENCE_DESIGN only with DEFAULT_ALLOWED, ALLOWED_EXCEPTION_EXPRESSION or OPEN_CONTENT, and the probe 'phoenix as REFERENCE_DESIGN' is rejected. Only the index and planned-baseline parts of the sentence match the data (langfuse, ai-boost/awesome-harness-engineering, EvoMap/awesome-agent-evolution). The reference-design case holds only for open content (claudes-c-compiler).

Residual limits. None affects the current data; all eight licenceStatedInPaper values are correct (see checksRun).
(a) licenceStatedInPaper is hard-coded in the builder and not cross-checked. The probe accepted true for MASS, whose only licence check is NOT_FOUND, and for VeriHarness, whose detail says NOT_FOUND for a licence.
(b) The new statusDetail rule is lexical. A detail saying the licence was verified passes, and the spelling 'license' in a claim bypasses the rule.
(c) Hygiene. '(at)' and '[at] … [dot]' obfuscations are not matched. The broadened 'x at domain' rule also flags legitimate site references such as 'available at veriharness.com.'; the record already rephrases around this twice.
(d) Bare names and free-form prompt residue remain review-only, which is accepted.
(e) Two optional wording points:
  - DESIGN_REFERENCE_ONLY says 'open content used as code', but ceiling() applies to all open content. Keeping open content as design-reference-only is acceptable, but the definition text should match it.
  - The meaning of roadmapCheck.license null ('no SPDX identifier', covering the roadmap's 'unknown' and 'NONE (no licence file)') is not stated in the record.

dispositions.evidence: VeriHarness check 9 now reads 'A released rollout corpus and code; a licence statement.', with the statusDetail 'VERIFIED for the code and the rollout corpus; NOT_FOUND for a licence (pp. 1, 22)'. Round 2 confirmed there is no licence text on pp. 1 or 22; the only licence on p. 21 is the MIT licence of a dependency. Every seed paper now has licenceStatedInPaper false, and the README status table shows a 'Licence stated in the paper' column ('no' for all eight). I grepped all 249 PDF pages and no paper states a licence for its own code or data. The only hits are HarnessDev's third-party licences (pp. 6, 22), a verb use in JAZ (p. 14) and VeriHarness's MIT dependency (p. 21). The MASS claim 5 statusDetail now follows its cleaned text. The new checker rule rejects a removed or licence-free detail on VeriHarness 9 and JAZ 6. Its limits are in R3-2 (a) and (b).

The precedence sentence was appended to LICENSE_BLOCKED, and REUSE_AFTER_GATES gained 'The ceiling binds whatever the reuse mode.' The index and planned-baseline parts now explain langfuse and the two NOASSERTION awesome lists. The reference-design part is too broad and contradicts five LICENSE_BLOCKED records and REUSE_OUTCOMES (R3-1).
